tasks.desc: Ideation: identify noncrossing matching model, even-block sorted-half-difference formula, and odd-N survivor split at odd original positions.
Implement standalone Python 3 two-heap prefix/suffix solution with correct stdin/stdout.
Validate samples and small brute-force cases; confirm O(N log N) complexity for N up to 3e5.

proposals: Validate the odd-N counterexample and the survivor-split idea with small-N brute force or interval DP.
Pursue the matching reduction: even blocks reduce to sorted-half-difference; odd N reduces to maximizing left-block value plus right-block value over valid survivor positions.
Implement prefix and suffix half-difference values using two heaps that maintain the smallest half and largest half of the current multiset.
Consider an alternative Fenwick-tree implementation over compressed values, querying the sum of the k smallest elements for each even prefix and suffix.
Use the sign-assignment/rearrangement view to double-check the proof and to ensure no cross-survivor pairing is being counted.
Test greedy adjacent-max only as a heuristic or counterexample generator, not as the final algorithm.
Keep optimized interval DP or Monge analysis as a fallback only if the split reduction fails on small cases.
prev: Write a fresh, complete Python 3 program (not a patch) that reads stdin, computes the answer with the validated formula: for every even prefix/suffix maintain lower/upper halves with two heaps and record sum_upper - sum_lower; for even N print pref[N//2]; for odd N print max_{t=0..N//2} pref[t] + suff[N//2-t]; ensure it writes the integer to stdout with a newline; then run the three samples and a brute-force interval DP for all N<=9 random arrays to verify, and include the final code in the required delimiters.
